newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas says to alter management structure.
newsitem.headline: Qantas says to alter management structure.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Monday it would restructure its senior management with effect from June 1, as part of an ongoing cost cutting programme.

The changes will reduce the number of divisions at the airline from four to six by merging the operations unit and associated business unit into other areas, chief executive James Strong said in a statement.
Ian Oldmeadow, the head of operations, and Norman Fricker, head of associated business, would leave Qantas in July after the transfer of responsibilities, Strong said.
Both men would remain available for consulting work.
Strong said the changes had been made to ensure management and overhead costs were reduced in line with efforts to improve efficiency and productivity throughout the group.
Under the changes, finance director and Qantas board member Gary Toomey will take responsibility for airports, freight and catering as well as finance.
Day-to-day activities within finance will be co-ordinated by George Dalidakis who will report to Toomey.
Qantas said Geoff Dixon would add in-flight services and resorts to his exisiting commercial portfolio.
Doug Gillies would take responsibility for industrial relations, human relations and regional airlines in addition to aircraft operations and engineering and maintenance.
David Burden would take over purchasing and property in addition to information technology.
A Qantas spokesman declined to put a figure on cost savings expected to flow from the changes.
Strong said on Sunday he expected Qantas to exceed its cost-cut target for the year to June 30, 1997, last estimated by the company at A$340 million.
Aviation analysts expect Qantas to save about A$500 million in spending during the 1996/97 financial year.
